title: India’s cotton sowing trails last year, Gujarat boosts outlook
summary:
India’s cotton sowing remains below last year’s level, with acreage at 7.51 lakh hectares versus 9.72 lakh hectares a year ago.
North India is expected to see lower cotton area as farmers shift to alternative crops.
However, strong planting growth in Gujarat, higher MSP and expectations of increased acreage in Central India are supporting optimism for the 2026-27 season.

title: Bangladesh–Türkiye textile talks: $876 mn trade corridor fuels FTA
summary:
Bangladesh–Türkiye trade talks offer an opportunity to combine Bangladesh’s apparel scale with Türkiye’s strengths in fibre, yarn and finishing. 
While apparel dominates bilateral trade, resilient yarn exports highlight deeper supply-chain links. 
The success of any FTA/PTA will depend more on investment, sourcing flexibility and value-chain integration than tariff cuts alone.

title: Grasim Industries announces fresh $309 mn Lyocell capacity expansion
summary:
Grasim Industries will invest ₹3,094 crore (~$309.4 million) to add 110,000 tonnes per annum (TPA) of Lyocell capacity at Harihar, Karnataka, through two new production lines scheduled for commissioning by 2028 and 2030. 
Combined with its ongoing 55,000 TPA Phase I project, Grasim’s total Lyocell capacity will reach nearly 210,000 TPA, strengthening its leadership in sustainable cellulosic fibres.

title: Asian PTA prices rise as polyester demand boosts buying
summary:
Asian PTA prices rose across China, South Korea, India and Southeast Asia, supported by stronger polyester demand and inventory replenishment. 
DTY filament yarn markets showed mixed trends, with export demand remaining firmer than domestic consumption. 
PTA gains outpaced DTY price increases, indicating margin pressure on yarn producers as feedstock costs continue to climb.

title: ICE cotton futures show mixed trend after hitting two-month lows
summary:
ICE cotton futures remained under pressure as rising certified stocks and speculative liquidation weighed on sentiment.
July futures slipped to 73.30 cents/lb, while December posted slight gains.
Trading volume exceeded 106,000 contracts, reflecting heavy fund unwinding.
Improved US crop conditions and ample certified stocks kept the outlook bearish, especially for nearby contracts.

title: India launches portal to operationalise Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana
summary:
Indian Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal yesterday launched a portal to operationalise the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA), which aims at developing 100 industrial parks to promote large-scale job creation through greater investments.
Through the portal, investors can access detailed information on industrial parks like land availability, connectivity and surrounding infrastructure.

title: Chinese, Cambodian customs ink AEO pact to streamline trade procedures
summary:
The customs authorities of China and Cambodia recently signed an authorised economic operator agreement to facilitate trade by simplifying customs procedures, accelerate customs clearance for highly compliant businesses and reduce physical inspections of goods. 
Cambodia has 11 AEO companies and its government is working to raise that number to 30, by the end of this year.

title: Europe’s industrial prices climb further in April: Eurostat
summary:
Industrial producer prices in April 2026 rose by 0.6 per cent MoM in the euro area and 0.7 per cent in the EU, according to the Eurostat. 
Annual producer inflation reached 4.9 per cent in both regions, driven mainly by energy prices, which surged over 12 per cent YoY. 
Denmark, Croatia and Belgium recorded the strongest monthly increases, while Bulgaria led annual producer price growth.

title: Australia’s Q1 growth moderates amid export disruptions
summary:
Australia’s GDP grew 0.3 per cent QoQ and 2.5 per cent YoY in Q1 2026, according to ABS data. 
Growth slowed due to weaker government spending, cautious household consumption and weather-related export disruptions. 
Exports fell 1.1 per cent, while private business investment surged 6 per cent, supported by data centre expansion projects. 
Household spending rose 0.5 per cent.

title: Italy’s GDP expected to grow 0.7% in both 2026, 2027: Istat
summary:
Italy’s GDP is expected to grow by 0.7 per cent in both 2026 and 2027 following a 0.5-per cent rise in 2025, according to Istat.
Employment is expected to record slower growth of 0.7 per cent this year after a 1.3-per cent growth last year, accompanied by a further decline in the unemployment rate.
In 2027, unemployment rate is expected to stabilise. 
Inflation is projected to rise sharply during 2026.

title: Workers' safety, apparel trade at risk from extreme heat: NYU
summary:
Extreme heat is fast turning one of the most serious threats to worker safety and supply chain resilience in the global apparel industry, a NYU Stern Center for Business and Human Rights report said.
Rising temperatures and humidity are already disrupting factory output, reducing productivity, damaging product quality, harming worker health and driving up absenteeism across South and Southeast Asia.

title: Can technical apparel be fashion’s next billion-dollar opportunity?
summary:
Technical apparel is evolving from a niche segment into a mainstream growth driver, fuelled by climate adaptation, health monitoring and wearable technology. 
Advances in smart textiles, sensors and performance materials are transforming garments into functional, data-enabled products. 
For manufacturers, this shift creates opportunities in higher-value, innovation-led markets.

title: Guatemala’s apparel exports reach $385 mn in Q1; knitwear dominates
summary:
Guatemala’s apparel exports rose 8.75 per cent year on year to $385.08 million in the first quarter of 2026, driven by strong US demand.
Knitwear accounted for over 91 per cent of shipments, while cotton apparel contributed nearly 62 per cent.
The US remained the dominant market, absorbing almost 90 per cent of exports, underscoring Guatemala’s strong dependence on its northern trading partner.

title: Tiruppur garment exports top $4.4 bn despite global trade challenges
summary:
Tiruppur’s garment exports stood at ₹42,544.40 crore ($4.4 billion) in fiscal 2025-26, down 4.91 per cent year on year due to US tariff issues and disruptions from the West Asia crisis, according to TEA.
Despite the decline, the knitwear hub remained resilient and sees growth opportunities through FTAs, MMF garments, sustainability initiatives, and rising export demand.

title: Cambodia’s clean-power garment premium
summary:
Cambodia is positioning clean energy as a sourcing advantage for its apparel industry, with renewables accounting for over 62 per cent of the power mix and solar capacity expanding rapidly. 
Energy audits highlight major cost and emissions-saving opportunities for factories. 
However, realising this potential will require wider renewable power access, financing, and credible low-carbon certification.

title: Australia’s apparel imports down 3.3%, textile import up in July-April
summary:
Australia’s apparel imports fell 3.3 per cent to Au$10.72 billion during July 2025-April 2026, while textile yarn, fabric and made-up article imports rose 1.6 per cent to Au$3.93 billion, according to ABS data.
Textile fibre imports also increased.
However, April 2026 saw declines in both apparel and textile imports, while textile fibre exports grew 4.9 per cent in the ten-month period.

title: Why Bangladesh RMG exporters feel April data needs July reality check
summary:
Bangladesh’s export earnings surged 32.92 per cent year on year in April, crossing the $4 billion mark, with apparel exports rising 31.21 per cent. 
However, exporters estimate actual growth at around 8–10 per cent, attributing the jump largely to delayed shipments after Eid disruptions.  
Industry stakeholders believe the true export trend will become clearer by July 2026.

title: Vietnam’s textile, garment exports reach $15.1 bn in January-May
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and garment exports (excluding yarn and fibre) edged up 0.4 per cent year-on-year to $15.13 billion during January-May 2026, while yarn exports rose 8.7 per cent to $1.89 billion.
Cotton imports fell 6.3 per cent in value despite higher volumes, and fabric imports eased 0.5 per cent.
The country is targeting $50 billion in textile, garment, and yarn exports in 2026.

title: US’ Torrid Q1 FY26 sales fall 7.6% despite guidance beat
summary:
Torrid Holdings reported first-quarter FY26 net sales of $245.8 million, down 7.6 per cent year-on-year, while net income fell to $0.4 million from $5.9 million. 
Comparable sales declined 1.7 per cent and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $17.6 million. 
The company closed 20 stores during the quarter and expects FY26 net sales between $940 million and $960 million.

title: Bangladesh garment exports slip to $35.3 bn in July-May
summary:
Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports fell 3.41 per cent year-on-year to $35.31 billion during July 2025-May 2026, with knitwear exports down 4.26 per cent and woven garments down 2.42 per cent.
Home textile exports rose 3.48 per cent to $853.26 million, while cotton product exports declined 11.23 per cent.
RMG and home textiles accounted for 82.57 per cent of the country’s total exports.
